text:
marta: Quick recap — I rolled out a small canary for P95 SLO-driven batching: dynamic token_budget targets per route/tier. The idea is to shrink budgets for low-tier routes and give headroom to premium routes. Observing perf and cache interplay now.

simone: Nice. Which signals are we using to set targets? p95 latency + current queue length?

marta: p95 measured over 1m windows + recent queue latency distribution. We map to a budget scalar per tier. Config snippet: 

```yaml
batching:
  slo: p95
  window: 60s
  route_tiers:
    premium: {target_ms: 120, base_budget: 1200}
    standard: {target_ms: 220, base_budget: 900}
    dev: {target_ms: 450, base_budget: 500}

budget_adjustment:
  algorithm: proportional
  max_step_pct: 0.2
```

marta: The runtime also chooses kernel variants depending on seq_len and model stage; wanted to call out a regression: one of the recent kernel selector heuristics bumped p95 on a couple of standard routes in canary.

paul: I saw that in tracing — the kernel switch added ~6ms per token on some seq_len=1 hot paths. We might be re-evaluating kernels too late (after batching decision).

zach: Can you paste the flame trace? I think pre-selecting preferred kernel at request enqueue time might avoid the mid-batch switch.

paul: Here — truncated trace from canary: 

```
# flame summary
runtime.loop -> batch.form -> kernel_selector.select (12ms) -> kernel.load_if_missing (30ms) -> attention_kernel.exec (120ms)
```

paul: Most of the extra cost is in kernel.load_if_missing when a cache miss for a compiled kernel happens.

simone: That's the kernel compilation / JIT path? We should ensure our kernel cache gets warmed before canary traffic hits those sequences. Maybe prefetch commonly used kernels for premium models.

marta: Agreed. Also KV cache behavior surfaced: dynamic budgets cause some requests to hit longer because KV cache warmups for long chats take tokens that push queues. For premium routes we keep a higher base_budget to prefer cache hits. For dev routes, small budgets can evict useful KV entries.

ryan: Do we have metrics for KV hit ratio by tier after the rollout?

marta: Quick numbers from the canary (1h window): premium KV hit 78%, standard 61% (down from 68% baseline), dev 39%. So standard dropped ~7pp — probably from lower budgets and higher eviction churn.

zach: That's concerning. Lower token budgets reduce per-request latency but can increase downstream latency when cache misses cascade. It becomes a non-linear tradeoff.

simone: Suggestion: make budget adjustment aware of per-route KV hit ratio. If hit ratio falls >5pp we temporarily relax budget until the cache stabilizes.

marta: Nice. Proposed rule: budget_scale *= (1 + alpha * max(0, target_hit - current_hit)). alpha=0.5 as starting point. Also cap adjustment per-step to avoid oscillation.

paul: Implementation note: we should instrument a lightweight fast-path in the runtime to estimate per-route KV hit ratio without scanning the whole cache — sampled counters updated on KV lookup.

infra-bot: Canary deployment 1918765400 -> 1918765600: batcher-v3 (10% traffic) rolled out. Monitors: p95 latency, kv_hit_ratio, kernel_cache_misses.

marta: After we enabled KV-aware budget adjustments, p95 for standard routes moved back towards baseline (210ms from 240ms). Premium remained stable. Dev routes improved latency a bit but throughput dropped — expected.

zach: Any regressions on tail? We should watch p99.

marta: p99 bumped slightly on mixed-length routes initially (from 480 -> ~520) but after pre-warming kernel cache for top 5 kernels it returned. Steps we took: precompile top kernels on startup, sample-based KV hit feedback loop, and delayed kernel selection until enqueue with prefetching for most-likely variants.

simone: Can we add a guard that if kernel_cache_miss_rate > 0.05, temporarily schedule small background compile tasks to catch up?

paul: We do have a background compiler, but it's low-priority. I'll raise its budget when canary signals high miss rate. Need to be careful not to starve other compiles.

marta: Action items:
- paul: add sampled KV counters per-route (low overhead) — due EOD tomorrow
- zach: add pre-warm list + boot precompile for top kernels for premium models — due 2d
- simone: formalize budget->kv_hit feedback formula and run offline sims — due 3d
- ryan: extend dashboards with kv_hit_ratio by tier and kernel_cache_miss_rate by region — due 2d

ryan: I'll add alert rules: kv_hit_ratio drop > 6pp for 5m for standard/premium -> warn; kernel_cache_miss_rate > 8% for 2m -> page.

marta: Thanks. We'll keep the canary running with those mitigations and reconvene after 24h. Short notes in #perf-daily. :rocket:

zach: Minor note — when you post the sim data, include seq_len distribution. The selector logic is very seq_len-sensitive.

marta: Will do.

paul: One more quick log snippet showing the budget adjust event (from runtime logs):

```
[2026-03-16T14:22:31Z] route=standard tier=standard p95=238ms target=220ms old_budget=900 new_budget=990 adj=+10% reason=kv_hit_drop(0.06)
```

marta: Perfect. End of thread for now.
